primitives.note: Arcane Mastery converts AP into bonus max mana (10% per 100 AP), and that bonus mana in turn feeds the 'bonus mana' ratio terms in Q/W/E's damage calcs.
Overload, Rune Prison, and Spell Flux each deal a flat+ratio magic damage instance on cast/short delay.
Every W or E cast resets Overload's cooldown, letting Q be recast far more often than its own 5s cooldown.
Spell Flux marks the target (and, in a multi-target scene, nearby enemies) with a 4s 'Flux' debuff that Ryze's other basic abilities read/consume for bonus effects.
Overload deals amplified damage when it hits a Flux-marked target (magnitude and whether Realm Warp rank gates it is unsettled).
Mana costs (especially W 50-90 and E 35-75, cast every few seconds) can meaningfully cap total casts inside a 15s window depending on Ryze's mana pool/regen at the tested level/items.
Realm Warp's passive increases Overload/Spell Flux empowered damage; it only exists once R has at least one point (i.e. champion level 6+).

needsBespoke.why: The kit's damage-relevant behaviors (flat+ratio hits, a cooldown reset chain between Q and W/E, a target mark that conditionally amplifies one ability's damage, mana costs as a soft cap, and a level-gated passive amp) are each expressible with existing primitives; the main difficulty is picking correct numbers, which is captured as unsettled questions rather than requiring new mechanic logic.

unsettled.question: What is the correct magnitude/index for Overload's damage bonus against a Spell Flux-marked target, and does it require Realm Warp to be ranked at all?
options: Bin is authoritative: RyzeQWrapper.DamageAmp = 40/50/60/70/80% keyed to Overload's own rank, applied regardless of whether R is ranked

Wiki's Overload page pp lookup is authoritative: 25/50/75/100% keyed to Realm Warp's rank (0-3), meaning at R rank 0 the bonus may be 0% or 25%, and the effect changes as R levels rather than as Q levels

Realm Warp's own leveling table (50/75/100% for R ranks 1-3) is the true 'Bonus Overload Damage' value, additively or multiplicatively stacked on top of a separate baseline Flux-bonus that exists independent of R
quotes: ''Overload'' deals {{pp|type=[[File:Realm Warp.png|20px|border]] ''Realm Warp's'' Rank|key=%|25 to 100 for 4|0 to 3}} {{ccs|increased damage|magic}} and spreads to surrounding ''Fluxed'' enemies.

unsettled.question: In the single-target dummy fight, does casting W or E on the dummy while it is already Flux-marked from a prior E cast retrigger/refresh the same debuff instance (extra value) or is the second application simply redundant since there is only one target and no bounce spread to model?
options: Re-casting E on an already-Flux target both deals a new damage instance and refreshes the mark, exactly as on the wiki, with no additional interaction in a 1-target scene
The 'triggers the previous one' note implies some additional proc (e.g., a second damage tick) beyond a simple refresh, which is unclear from the wording alone
quotes: ''Spell Flux's'' second cast on a target will apply a new ''Flux'' debuff as well as triggering the previous one (effectively refreshing the duration).

proposal: Open with Spell Flux (E) on the dummy to apply the Flux mark and land its own magic damage.
Immediately follow with Overload (Q), which is amplified by the fresh Flux mark and whose cast also does not consume its own cooldown reset opportunity from W/E.
Cast Rune Prison (W) next; this both deals its own damage and resets Overload's cooldown, letting Q be cast again right away.
Recast Overload (Q) again off the reset cooldown.

Repeat the E -> Q -> W -> Q cycle continuously for the full ~15s, re-applying Spell Flux roughly every time its own (short, 2.5-3.5s) cooldown is up so Overload keeps benefiting from the Flux amplification, and using every W/E cast purely to keep chaining free Overload casts.

Do not cast Realm Warp (R): it deals no direct damage itself, has a long channel that would forfeit multiple Q/W/E casts, and its only offensive contribution is the passive Overload-damage amp, which is already accounted for passively once ranked.
questions: Should Realm Warp be assumed ranked (level 6+) for the passive Overload/Flux damage amp even though R itself is never cast in the 15s fight, and if so at what rank given the tested champion level?

Which of the conflicting Flux-amplification value sets (bin's per-Q-rank array vs wiki's per-R-rank lookup vs Realm Warp's own leveling table) should the simulator use for Overload's bonus damage vs a Flux target?

Is Ryze assumed to start the fight with full mana, and does the target dummy's mana pool/regen at the tested level make the E/W mana costs a real constraint over 15s, or is mana effectively unlimited given typical AP+mana itemization?

Does buffering Overload during the E/W cast time (explicitly called out in the wiki notes) let it fire with zero effective downtime between the E/W cast finishing and Q firing, i.e. should the simulated cast sequence treat Q as free time-wise whenever chained after W/E?
